title: Variant-specific GPU footprint allocator and KV residency tuning for long-context inference
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Reduce per-model GPU resident footprint and improve KV cache residency for long-sequence workloads by creating variant-aware allocator heuristics and an adaptive residency policy. This ticket covers: (1) collecting per-variant memory signatures across Llama/Mistral/Qwen families for 8k/32k/64k contexts, (2) synthesizing a compact allocator that adjusts slab/span allocations and KV placement based on sequence distribution, and (3) integrating a lightweight runtime policy that prefers partial eviction vs. full reallocation during continuous batching bursts.

Why: Current generic allocator overprovisions for several model variants under long-context use, causing either wasted memory headroom or forcing fallbacks to smaller model variants. We need an automated way to tune residency so latency SLOs are met while increasing effective capacity per GPU.

Scope: This is an engineering task requiring runtime instrumentation, benchmark harness updates, a small compatibility shim in the serving runtime, and a rollout plan for canarying on Dedicated pools. The outcome should be a parameterized allocator with a short profile lookup table per model-variant and a residency policy that: (a) keeps hot KV cache entries pinned during streaming, (b) opportunistically compresses low-utility slabs, and (c) falls back gracefully with predictable latency degradation.

Non-goals: Model quantization changes, end-user API changes, major on-disk format migrations.

Deliverables: profile collection scripts, profile dataset (per-variant per-context), allocator prototype, benchmark results, GitHub PRs with tests and perf dashboards, rollout runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Allocator prototype is merged behind feature flag and passes unit tests in CI
Per-variant profile table created for Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B, Qwen-14B for 8k/32k/64k contexts and stored in /profiles/runtime/variant-signatures
On the benchmark harness, average tokens/sec per GPU for long-seq chat workloads increases by >= 8% for at least two of the three target variants without violating 99th percentile latency SLO
KV residency policy reduces full KV evictions during sustained bursts by >= 40% on synthetic multi-session load
Runbook includes canary thresholds, automatic rollback criteria, and monitoring queries for token throughput, memory pressure, and eviction counts
steps: Add instrumentation hooks to collect slab/arena/KV allocation histograms per model variant and sequence length
Run full-profile sweep on infra pool (small GPU fleet) for Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants at 8k/32k/64k and record traces
Analyze traces to derive compact signature (cold-resident, stream-growth-rate, worst-case KV expansion)
Design allocator heuristics: slab resizing factors, preferred KV residency thresholds, and transient eviction window sizing
Implement allocator behind runtime feature flag and add config APIs for profile lookup
Integrate lightweight residency controller that hooks into batching events to decide pin/evict/compress
Benchmark on harness and compare against baseline; iterate heuristics
Prepare PR, perf dashboards, and operator runbook for canary rollout
benchmarks: Baseline (master): Llama-2-13B 32k chat mixed load: 1800 tokens/sec (avg), 99th lat = 210ms, full-KV-evictions = 120/hr
Target: +8% tokens/sec (>=1944 tokens/sec) while 99th lat <= 230ms and full-KV-evictions <= 72/hr
Mistral-7B baseline 64k streaming: 950 tokens/sec, aim for +12% with identical latency envelope
Qwen-14B baseline 32k bursty: 1400 tokens/sec, aim for +7% and 40% fewer full evictions
risks: Allocator misprediction could increase fragmentation and degrade multi-tenant density
Profile table may not generalize across microarchitecture (A100v4 vs H100) — need per-hardware variants
Eviction policy complexity could add jitter to tail latency if not throttled
Rollback requires careful state reconciliation to avoid leaving partially-evicted KV entries
